title: Processing of identified data during parent registration
description: The Authentication Service explicitly requests and processes identified personal data including email, name, and government ID during parent registration. This identified data directly reveals the identity of the data subject.
assumptions: The registration flow requires explicit identification of the parent user

title: Unique identifiers in registration data
description: The registration data contains unique references to the identity of the data subject, including email address and government ID, which serve as direct identifiers.
assumptions: Email and government ID are unique to each parent user

title: Linking through unique identifiers
description: The email, government ID, and six-digit code can serve as unique identifiers that enable linking of this parent's data across different systems or within the authentication service over time.
assumptions: These identifiers are used consistently across the system

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination
description: The combination of name, email, and government ID creates a quasi-identifier set that can uniquely identify and link data to a specific parent user even if individual identifiers are not used.
assumptions: The combination of these attributes is unique to each parent

title: Collection of highly sensitive government ID data
description: Government ID is a highly sensitive data type that may not be functionally required for parent registration. This exceeds what might be necessary for basic authentication purposes.
assumptions: Government ID collection may be more sensitive than required for the stated functionality
uncertainty_note: Uncertainty about whether govt ID is functionally necessary for this registration flow

title: Excessive amount of personal data collected
description: Multiple personal data points are collected during registration (email, password, name, government ID, six-digit code), which may exceed what is functionally needed for parent authentication.
assumptions: All five data elements are collected in a single registration flow

title: Attributable registration data
description: The registration data can be used to attribute the registration action to a specific parent user, preventing them from denying their registration or associated claims.
assumptions: Registration data is stored and can be used as evidence

title: Unawareness of data processing scope
description: Parent users may not be fully aware of how their registration data (especially government ID) will be processed, stored, or disclosed beyond the immediate authentication purpose.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not fully explain all processing activities
uncertainty_note: Depends on quality of privacy notices provided to users

title: Lack of control over data processing preferences
description: Parent users may have limited ability to set preferences or provide granular consent for how their registration data is processed, particularly for sensitive data like government ID.
assumptions: Registration flow may use all-or-nothing consent model

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Collecting government ID and multiple data points during registration may violate the GDPR data minimization principle if all data is not strictly necessary for the authentication functionality.
assumptions: GDPR or similar regulations apply to this system
uncertainty_note: Depends on whether govt ID is functionally necessary for the stated purpose

title: JWT contains unique identifier
description: The JWT token transmitted in this flow contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject, enabling identification of the user.
assumptions: JWT tokens typically contain user identification claims

title: User data contains revealing attributes
description: The user data transmitted alongside the JWT may contain revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject.
assumptions: User data typically includes personally identifiable information

title: JWT enables linking through unique identifier
description: The JWT token serves as a unique identifier that can be used to link data across different systems or contexts.
assumptions: JWT tokens are designed to be unique and persistent

title: Signed JWT prevents deniability
description: JWT tokens are typically cryptographically signed, which can prevent the data subject from denying their authentication actions.
assumptions: JWT tokens are signed by the authentication service

title: Potentially sensitive user data disclosed
description: The user data transmitted may include sensitive personal information beyond what is functionally required for the parent user.
assumptions: User data may contain sensitive attributes
uncertainty_note: Depends on what specific user data is included

title: Data shared with predetermined party
description: Personal data is made accessible to the parent user, which is a predetermined party in this system context.
assumptions: Parent user is a known, fixed party in the system

title: Data subject unaware of processing
description: The actual data subject (e.g., child/student) may not be aware that their personal data is being shared with the parent user through this flow.
assumptions: Data subject may be different from the parent user receiving the data
uncertainty_note: Depends on system design and consent mechanisms

title: Lack of data subject preferences control
description: The data subject may lack control over which personal data is shared with the parent user and how it is processed.
assumptions: Data subject may not have preference settings for data sharing

title: Potential violation of data minimization
description: The flow may transmit more personal data than is actually needed for the parent user's legitimate purposes.
assumptions: User data may include unnecessary fields
uncertainty_note: Depends on what specific data is transmitted

title: Processing of identified data during child login
description: The Authentication Service processes identified data (parent email and password) to authenticate the child user. This involves direct processing of personally identifiable information.
assumptions: Standard authentication flow where credentials are transmitted and verified

title: Identifier in login credentials
description: The parent email serves as a unique reference to the identity of the data subject (parent account holder), which is linked to the child user's access.
assumptions: Parent email is used as a unique identifier for account authentication

title: Linking through unique identifier
description: The parent email can be used to link the child's login activity and subsequent system usage to a specific parent account and child profile.
assumptions: Email is stored and used as a linking key across system components

title: Sensitive data type collection
description: Passwords are highly sensitive data types being collected during the login process. This exceeds what might be minimally necessary if alternative authentication methods were available.
assumptions: Password-based authentication is the primary or only method

title: Implicit data disclosure during authentication
description: The login process may implicitly collect additional data such as device information, IP address, location, and timing data as side-effects of the authentication flow.
assumptions: Standard web authentication captures metadata alongside credentials

title: Attributable login data
description: Login credentials and authentication records can be used to attribute actions and access to the child user (via parent account), preventing denial of access or usage.
assumptions: Authentication logs are maintained and can be traced to specific users

title: Child unawareness of data processing
description: The child user may not be fully aware of what personal data is collected, processed, and stored during the login process, including metadata and authentication logs.
assumptions: Children may not read or understand privacy notices during login

title: Invalid consent for child data processing
description: Children may not be able to provide valid consent for data processing. Parental consent mechanisms may be insufficient or not properly implemented for this authentication flow.
assumptions: Child users are under age of consent and require parental authorization
uncertainty_note: Depends on jurisdiction and specific age thresholds for children

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: Collecting full passwords rather than using secure hashing or alternative authentication methods may violate data minimization principles, especially for child users.
assumptions: Passwords are stored or transmitted in a way that exceeds functional necessity
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual implementation of password storage

title: JWT Token Enables Linking Across Sessions

assumptions: JWT tokens are unique and persistent across sessions

title: JWT Contains Unique User Identifier

assumptions: JWT includes user identification claims

title: Child Profile Contains Revealing Attributes

title: Signed JWT Prevents Deniability

title: Sensitive Child Profile Data Disclosed

title: Child User Unaware of Profile Data Processing

title: Invalid Consent for Child Data Processing

title: Child profiling through search and watch history

description: The MongoDB childprofiles collection likely contains unique identifiers (child IDs, user IDs) that enable linking of search and watch history data to specific children across the system.
assumptions: Child profiles contain unique identifiers linking to child identities

title: Processing of identified child data
description: The child profile management process requests and processes identified data including child search and watch history, which is directly associated with identifiable children.
assumptions: Child profiles contain identified rather than anonymized data

title: Unique identifiers in stored child profiles
description: The MongoDB collection contains unique references to child identities, enabling identification of data subjects from the stored search and watch history.

title: Sensitive child behavioral data collection
description: Search and watch history of children is highly sensitive personal data that reveals interests, preferences, and potentially concerning content exposure. This data type may be more sensitive than functionally required.

title: Extended retention of child behavioral data

title: Children unaware of data collection
description: Children as data subjects may not be aware that their search and watch history is being collected, processed, and stored in the child profiles system.

title: Lack of child control over data erasure

title: Video content streamed to child user
description: Personal data (video content) is made accessible to a predetermined party (the child user). While this is the intended function, streaming video to children requires careful consideration of content appropriateness and data exposure to vulnerable populations.
assumptions: The video content may contain personal data or be considered sensitive when delivered to a child user

title: Child unaware of data processing during video streaming
description: The child user may not be fully aware of what data is being collected, processed, or disclosed during the video streaming session, including viewing patterns, device information, or interaction data.

title: Child lacks control over data processing preferences
description: The child user may lack the ability to set preferences or provide meaningful consent regarding how their personal data is processed during video streaming, which is particularly concerning given their vulnerable status.

title: Invalid consent for child data processing

title: Potential violation of data minimization for child users
description: The system may collect or process more personal data than necessary when streaming video to children, violating the data minimization principle which is especially important for vulnerable populations.

title: Unique Identifiers in Child Profiles

title: Revealing Attributes in Browsing Data
description: Child browsing data contains revealing attributes (interests, behaviors, preferences) that support identification and profiling of children.

title: Individual profiling through browsing data
description: The AI Recommendation Engine sends browsing data to third-party advertisers, enabling them to analyze user behavior patterns and create detailed profiles of individuals for targeted advertising purposes.

title: Linking through unique identifiers in browsing data
description: Browsing data transmitted to advertisers likely contains unique identifiers (cookies, device IDs, session tokens) that enable linking of browsing activity across sessions and to specific individuals.

title: Quasi-identifiers in browsing data
description: Browsing data contains combinations of attributes (timing, location, content preferences, device characteristics) that can serve as quasi-identifiers to identify data subjects even without explicit identifiers.

title: Sensitive data types in browsing data
description: Browsing data may include sensitive information about health interests, financial activities, personal relationships, or other sensitive topics that exceed what is functionally necessary for advertising.

title: Data propagation to third-party advertisers
description: Personal browsing data is propagated to external third-party advertisers where it may be used beyond the original context and potentially shared further with additional parties.
assumptions: Third-party advertisers may further share or process the received data

title: Dynamic set of advertising parties
description: The third-party advertisers receiving browsing data may change dynamically, making it difficult to control or audit which parties have access to personal data.
assumptions: Advertiser relationships are not static and may change over time

title: User unawareness of browsing data sharing
description: Data subjects may not be fully aware that their browsing data is being shared with third-party advertisers, or may not understand the extent of data collection and sharing.

title: Lack of user control over data sharing preferences

title: Violation of data minimization principle

title: Invalid consent for third-party data sharing

title: JWT enables linking across sessions
description: JWT stored in localStorage contains user identifiers that can be used to link user activities across different sessions and potentially across different systems that accept the same JWT format.
assumptions: JWT contains user-identifying claims

title: JWT contains user identifier
description: The JWT stored in localStorage contains a unique reference to the identity of the data subject, allowing identification of the authenticated user.
assumptions: JWT includes user identity claims

title: JWT accessible to browser scripts
description: localStorage is accessible to any JavaScript running in the browser context, potentially exposing the JWT to malicious scripts through XSS attacks or third-party scripts.

title: JWT may persist longer than needed

title: Users unaware of JWT storage

title: Limited control over JWT removal

title: Potential storage limitation violation

assumptions: JWT expiration not enforced at storage level

title: Insufficient cybersecurity risk management
